caption: The drawing contains two main elements: an inset illustration at the top left and a detailed map occupying the majority of the composition. The inset illustration shows a two-story house with a chimney and wide porch, painted in light cream and tan tones, set amongst several tall, narrow trees with green and yellow foliage on green grass, with a curved red pathway leading to the entrance and bushes near the house; the sky is a light pastel blue with hints of purple and green trees in the background. Below and to the right, the main area displays a stylized bird's-eye map in predominantly green and blue watercolor representing trees and grassy land with various circular and curved shapes. At the center is a grey, rectangular roofed structure, perhaps representing a building. To the right of this structure are orderly rectangular garden plots filled with alternating colors of green, brown, and reddish rows suggesting different types of vegetation or crops, separated by white walkways. There are several additional small reddish and teal features suggesting smaller buildings or garden beds. Lighter paths snake and curve through the landscape, connecting the house, plots, and other features, dividing a mixture of densely treed and open spaces. The text "JOHN W. AUDUBON HOMESTEAD" and "THE BLACKWELL SURVEY" appears below the map. Handwritten notes are present at the bottom of the image, reading "John W. Audubon's Homestead" and further annotations lower right in pencil.
title: J. Audubon Estate
